I own a small business and here are my thoughts on this. Small transactions in cash are not likely to raise suspicions ($25-$30). However, my accountant requires me to file a 1099 form on anyone I pay more than $600 in a single year. So for example on your hypothetical company, a farm is a small business. They are going to put in their books that they paid $5000 to XYZ person or company to fix whatever. At the end of the year they will file a 1099 indicating that they did so. Here's where the trouble starts, if the person doing the maintenance claims enough income to cover all the 1099's he's received and been filed with the IRS, no problem. But, say if he made $200,000 in a year and other businesses filed 1099's in the amount of $150K on him but he only claimed a gross income of $100,000 because he was paid $100K in cash and simply put that in his pocket, that will set off a red flag in the computer and you'll get a letter from your friendly neighborhood IRS agent saying you're going to be audited. Now, I think the types of businesses that can get away with this the most are contractors that cater primarily to consumers (homeowners). Individuals are not required to file 1099 forms for work they've had done on their homes. So, people like lawn maintenance, painters, plumbers, handyman type workers can and most likely do pocket a lot of cash which they don't claim as income. However, you can still get caught if you deposit checks in your bank account. There are a bunch of screwy laws which I'm only aware of vaguely that require the banks to file reports to the IRS on all sorts of transactions. So you can still get caught. Also, this usually happens after they get interested in you, but if you live a lifestyle that doesn't match with the income you report, then you'll get caught as well. For example, you file a form incorrectly and get audited, happens all the time. The agent starts looking through your stuff and finds that you report $50K in earnings every year, but, you live in a $500K house, have three kids in private college, get a new Mercedes Benz every few years and go on lavish vacations to the tropics regularly, you really shouldn't have the money for all that, should you? You'll get busted, so my advise is it's best to report the money you earn and not raise the interest of anyone at the government. Make a lot of money pay your taxes and live well, it's the best revenge.
